trust_decision.summary: Which mail values a website visitor can influence may be used as Fluid template source, and which ViewHelpers a parsed string may run. Both are decided in SendMailService::getKeysAllowedToContainFluid() and RestrictedStringRenderer/ViewHelperPolicy. ALREADY PRESENT at the pinned commit.

landing_point.why: fluidParseString() is the one helper that turns a string into a Fluid template source, and every SSTI path in powermail runs through it

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unknown: the published fix diff contains no source change, so there is no site to dismiss

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Editor- or integrator-written subject, receiver and sender strings must keep resolving {marker} variables and f:cObject. RTE bodytext in VariablesViewHelper stays fully permissive (documented feature).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second StandaloneView::setTemplateSource() parse outside RestrictedStringRenderer, here for the RTE bodytext; a planted variant would put a visitor-influenced value into the source instead of assigning it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the code already keeps a permissive parse path next to the restricted one (Classes/Fluid/RestrictedStringRenderer.php:37-46), so a maintainer could add another 'trusted' parse that mixes in submitted data

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a field option label parsed with fluidParseString(); a sibling that parses visitor-supplied option values in the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the model already parses editor-written labels, and prefill or option values sit right beside them
